ITEM 1  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  A.  Election of Chair and Vice Chair

  Chair Villablanca stated that the election of Chair and Vice Chair would be
  postponed to the next Regular meeting, as Commissioner Peak was absent.

  Senior Center Program Presentation bV Recreation Coordinator Joie Cosentino

  Deputy Director Manisco introduced Recreation Coordinator Joie Cosentino and
  Part-Time Permanent Recreation Assistant H Raphael Winkler. She stated both
  employees worked at the Senior Center at Malibu City Hall.

  Recreation Coordinator Cosentino gave updates on the operation of the Senior
  Center, including an overview of programs, excursions, events, and the Dial-A-
  Ride program.

  In response to Commissioner Skophammer, Deputy Director Manisco stated that
  the census data was pulled from 2023, but the demographic numbers are projected
  for each year.

  In response to Commissioner Skophammer, Recreation Coordinator Cosentino
  stated that program offerings were based on participant feedback.

  In response to Commissioner Goldfarb, Recreation Coordinator Cosentino stated
  the walking group would meet at Malibu Bluffs Park before croquet and bocce ball
  classes begin.

ITEM 2  WRITTEN AND ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE PUBLIC

  Louise Greene thanked staff for planning a bocce ball program and for extending
  the time for the senior knitting group.

  Kevin Keegan stated he wanted to discuss programming ideas for Los Angeles
  2028 Olympic and to include discussions with the Harry Barovsky Memorial Youth
  Commission.

  Haley Rivers stated she was using the Malibu Equestrian Park for horse training
  lessons and wanted to ensure it remains part of the community.

  Sanaa Pharayra wanted to maintain public access to the Malibu Equestrian Park.
  She stated the park required maintenance; however, the equestrian community was
  present in Malibu.

  Haylynn Conrad complimented Senior Center staff for their hard work and for
  listening to participant feedback.

ITEM 3  CONSENT CALENDAR

MOTION  Vice Chair Lingo moved, and Commissioner Goldfarb seconded a motion to
  approve the consent calendar. The question was called, and the motion carried 4—0;
  Commissioner Peak absent.

ITEM 5  NEW BUSINESS

  Earth Friendly Management Policy Quarterly Update
  Recommended Action: Receive and file a report on the Earth Friendly Management
  Policy activities from July 2025 through December 2025.

  Recreation Manager Orosz presented the staff report.

  Commissioner Skophammer stated the City should be recognized for its
  participation and commitment to the Monarch Pledge.

  In response to Vice Chair Lingo, Recreation Manager Orosz stated gopher
  mitigation solutions would require a discussion with the parks division. He stated
  the reintroduction of gopher snakes could be done at Legacy Park.

  In response to Chair Villablanca. Recreation Manager Orosz stated that a permit
  from the State would be required to move a native species from one parcel to
  another.

  In response to Commissioner Skophammer, Recreation Manager Orosz stated that
  the Pepperdine University study was proposed because the students were seeking a
  solution to a problem already present.

  Commissioner Skophammer suggested applying for the special permit while the
  study was underway rather than waiting until it was completed.

  Commissioner Goldfarb suggested new invasive species signage for public
  education.

  Las Flores Creek Park Playground Replacement Proiect
  Recommended Action: Review and provide feedback on the Las Flores Creek Park
  playground design.

  Community Services Deputy Director Manisco presented the staff report.

  Scott Dittrich supported a new dog park at Las Flores Creek Park. He stated the
  playground was underutilized and suggested the Commission research park use and
  amenities before installing a new playground.

  Commissioner Goldfarb stated the old playground equipment was splintered and
  hoped the new equipment did not have that issue.

  In response to Commissioner Goldfarb, Community Services Deputy Director
  Manisco stated the rubber pour-in-place surface was required and made from
  recyclable material.

  Commissioner Skophammer stated the picnic tables were too far away from the
  playground and asked if they could be moved closer.

  In response to Commissioner Skophammer, Community Services Deputy Director
  Manisco stated the playground area could not accommodate swings due to the
  required fall zone.

  In response to Chair Villablanca, Community Services Deputy Director Manisco
  stated that the septic system was damaged during the Palisades Fire and it would
  be repaired during Phase 2 along with the playground.

MOTION  Commissioner Skophammer moved, and Chair Villablanca seconded a motion to
  approve the Las Flores Creek Park playground design. The question was called,
  and the motion carried 4-0; Commissioner Peak absent.

ITEM 6  STAFF UPDATES

  Community Services Deputy Director Manisco provided an update on the Chumash
  Day Powwow, Automated External Defibrillator (AED) installation, and the
  California Parks and Recreation Society (CPRS) 2025 Award of Excellence.

  Recreation Manager Orosz provided an update on the whale-watching telescopes
  at Malibu Bluffs Park and Outdoor Recreation programs.

  In response to Commissioner Goldfarb, Recreation Manager Orosz stated he would
  research the feasibility to install a telescope at a Charmlee Wildemess Park
  overlook.

Subject:  Youth Sports Organizations Facility Use

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Receive and file the 2025-26 annual report on youth sports
organization registrations and facility usage.

DISCUSSION: The Community Services Department works with youth sports
organizations throughout the year to provide field space at Malibu Bluffs Park and Trancas
Canyon Park, which allows over 594 youth athletes to use City facilities for soccer,
baseball, and softball. The primary youth sports organizations are Malibu American Youth
Soccer Organization (AYSO) and Malibu Little League (MLL), which provide youth
recreation leagues apart from City-organized programs. Additionally, the City works with
Views Football Club (Views FC), which is an elite club organization based in Malibu.

Malibu AYSO
AYSO’s regular season is from August to November for children ages 4 to 17. In 2025-
26, AYSO had 315 registered participants. The percentage of non-residents was
approximately 18% of the total number of registered participants. Non-residents come
from the nearby communities of Agoura Hills, Calabasas, Los Angeles, Santa Monica,
Thousand Oaks, and Unincorporated Los Angeles County.

 During the 2025-26 regular season, AYSO used Malibu Bluffs Park for practices and
games six days a week. Following the regular season, AYSO transitions to playoffs and
the all-star season, which begins the week after Thanksgiving and runs through January.
The weekly field space usage during the playoffs and all-star seasons was 30% to 40% of
the regular season. Additionally, AYSO hosts spring soccer from March through May, with
clinics on Sundays at Malibu Bluffs Park.

Malibu Little League
MLL organizes baseball and softball leagues that serve the Malibu area. Registration has
strict residency guidelines, and families must reside in Malibu or apply for a special permit
to participate in the league. ln 2026, MLL had 237 registered participants. The percentage
of non-resident participants was approximately 20% of the total number of registered
participants.

  MLL Season  Registered Participants
  2022  254
  2023  274
  2024  270
  2025  245
  2026  237

MLL installs temporary backstops on the Multipurpose Field at Malibu Bluffs Park, which
adds two modified baseball fields for younger players. During their 2026 season, MLL
offered Coach Pitch Baseball for the sixth consecutive year and Juniors Baseball (formerly
Pony Baseball) for the fifth year.

MLL’s regular season begins in February and continues through June, with all-star
practices following the regular season. MLL uses field space during the regular season for
practices and games seven days a week.

Additionally, MLL offers fall baseball from September to November. Practices and games
take place at Malibu Bluffs Park six days a week.

Additional Field Space Allocation
Since 2023, Views FC has coordinated an elite club soccer program at Malibu Bluffs Park
and Trancas Canyon Park for children ages 4 to 14. Views FC used City fields over the
past year, three days a week during the fall and one day a week during the spring. This
field use has reduced since 2023 when field use was up to six days a week during the fall
and four days a week during the spring.

 Summary of Field Use
In 2025-26, organized youth sports participation remained consistent with 2024-25. AYSO
registration remained the same, and MLL registration decreased by 3% compared to 2025.
Organizers believe this is attributed to the impacts from the Palisades and Franklin Fires.

Athletic fields at Malibu Bluffs Park are reserved at near maximum capacity for youth sports
leagues and City programs after 3:00 PM on weekdays and from 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM on
weekends. Permitted use at Trancas Canyon Park allows for practices Monday through
Friday, which was used exclusively by Views FC.

Rain affected the availability of fields throughout the winter and spring seasons. Weather-
related field closures at Malibu Bluffs Park and Trancas Canyon Park are listed below.

Subject:  Recreation Program, Events, and Park Maintenance Updates

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Discuss and recommend the format for receiving updates on
recreation programs, events, and park maintenance projects.

DISCUSSION: The Community Services Department utilizes a variety of report formats to
track recreation program attendance and park maintenance projects. Historically, the
Commission receives monthly reports which summarize participant registration numbers,
attendance trends, demographic data, program capacity utilization, and revenue
generated from recreation programs and special events. The monthly Commission report
offers a collective summary of program performance, while identifying community
interests, and supporting future planning efforts.

Park maintenance reports focus on daily park and facility maintenance and landscaping
efforts, project milestones, vandalism, and contractor performance. Recently, the
Department has incorporated photographs of project sites to ensure the project quality
complies with City goals and service standards.

Staff are requesting feedback from the Commission to determine if the current format of
the monthly report is preferred or ifthe Commission prefers a new format. The Commission
should consider report format such as text, graphs, charts, etc. in addition to frequency
such as monthly, quarterly, bi-annually, or annually.  Reports may include age
demographics, attendance/participation, revenue, photographs, instructor information,
and revenue tracking.
